note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 1 week of sore throat progressing to dry, nonproductive cough with exertional shortness of breath and mild wheeze; clinical impression consistent with viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis; supportive care, safety-netting, and a sick note provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sore throat for ~1 week, followed by a dry cough; interfering with work (missed 3–4 days).
- Timeline:
  - Sore throat began Thu/Fri last week.
  - Dry cough started 1–2 days later (Sat/Sun).
  - Exertional shortness of breath began ~3–4 days ago.
  - Initial fever during first ~3 days; now resolved.
  - Symptoms variable day-to-day; overall not progressively worsening; cough same day and night.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Shortness of breath with exertion (able to walk/exercise; not at rest).
  - No reported nocturnal worsening of cough.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Mild wheeze.
  - Chest discomfort/pain reported (“a bit of both” when asked about wheeze and chest pain); later the clinician re-queried suggesting no chest pain — conflict noted.
  - Intermittent headaches (currently absent).
  - Decreased appetite; no reported weight loss.
  - No nasal/sinus congestion.
  - No hemoptysis.
  - No rashes.
  - No neck lumps felt by patient.
- Other:
  - No recent significant travel beyond Europe; resides in UK; born in US.
  - Patient concerned about tuberculosis and cancer; seeking reassurance, advice, and a sick note.

Past Medical History:
- Denies known chronic medical conditions.
- No history of asthma noted.
- History of venous thromboembolism (VTE): not documented.

Medications:
- Current medications: None reported.
- Allergies: Peanuts. No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Employment: Employed; requested sick note for additional days off.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker; rare experimentation (“once or twice”).
- Asbestos exposure: Unknown.
- Alcohol/substance use: Not recorded.
- Residence/travel: Lives in UK; moved from US ~12 years ago; recent travel limited to Europe.

Family History:
- Mother: Lung cancer.
- Family history of VTE: Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Teleconsult; no in-person exam performed. Patient reports no palpable neck lumps. Otherwise not recorded.

Investigations:
- None ordered; no results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Most consistent with acute viral upper respiratory infection with associated acute bronchitis. Exertional dyspnea and subjective wheeze may represent post-viral reactive airway changes. No current red flags. Reassurance provided.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute viral URI with acute bronchitis (incl. COVID-19/influenza): Timeline of sore throat → dry cough, early fever now resolved, nonproductive cough; supports diagnosis. Opposes: exertional dyspnea/wheeze could suggest reactive airway disease.
  - Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma: Dry cough, wheeze, exertional dyspnea following viral illness support; opposes: no prior asthma, no nocturnal pattern, no objective testing.
  - Atypical/early community-acquired pneumonia: Early fever and chest discomfort could fit; opposes: now afebrile, non-productive cough, mild symptoms only, no exam/imaging.

- Issue 1: Acute cough and sore throat—suspected viral URI/acute bronchitis.
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic care: Paracetamol; fluids; rest (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - No antibiotics discussed.
    - Expect improvement over next 4–5 days.
    - Re-contact healthcare provider if not improving.

- Issue 2: Exertional shortness of breath and wheeze—likely post-viral airway hyperreactivity.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor symptoms.
    - Seek in-person GP assessment urgently if breathlessness worsens, occurs at rest, or there is a sudden change.
    - If persistent beyond expected recovery, arrange in-person evaluation.

- Issue 3: Work absence.
  - Plan:
    - Sick note provided for a few additional days off work.

- General plan items:
  - Safety-netting: If symptoms significantly worsen (especially dyspnea) or fail to improve as expected, seek in-person GP review.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No vitals, oxygen saturation, or physical examination findings.
  - No objective respiratory assessment (auscultation/peak flow).
  - No diagnostic testing discussed (e.g., COVID-19/influenza).
  - Medication dosing for paracetamol not documented.
  - Immunization status not recorded.
- Conflicts:
  - DOB recorded as 09-May-2016 vs adult social context (employment, independent travel, remote smoking experimentation) — conflict noted.
  - Shortness of breath initially denied, then affirmed.
  - Chest pain: patient initially agreed to “a bit” of chest pain; later question implied denial — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some incomplete/overlapping speech; teleconsult ended abruptly due to time; no physical exam performed.
